text: Mr. Frodo has sold Bag End to the Sackville-Bagginses, so they say, and for hardly any price at all.
Strange folk are passing along the East Road these days: tall, grim and in a hurry, and none will say whence they come.
Companies of Dwarves have been seen on the Road, tramping along with heavy packs and not stopping to talk.
A black-cloaked rider came to Bagshot Row asking the Gaffer after one Baggins, and sniffing like a hound.
Mr. Frodo has gone off at night with young Sam Gamgee and Master Peregrin, and no one knows where.
Elves were heard singing in the Woody End last night, a fair company going west.
A Black Rider rode up to Farmer Maggot's gate, and Maggot's dogs wouldn't stop barking for an hour.
The old Wizard Gandalf was seen riding a great white horse through Hobbiton, but he would not tarry.
Black riders on black horses have come to the West-gate of Bree asking for a Baggins.
A hobbit calling himself Underhill vanished clean out of the Pony's common room, so they say, right in the middle of a song.
Something broke into the Prancing Pony in the night and slashed the beds, and left a dreadful cold behind it.
The Horn of Buckland was blown in the night! Black riders came to Crickhollow and Fatty Bolger fled them.
Four hobbits left Bree this morning in the company of that Ranger, Strider, and a poor old pony from Bill Ferny.
Lobelia Sackville-Baggins has moved into Bag End at last and is counting the spoons.
They say fire was seen on Weathertop by night, and a cold cry that carried for leagues.
